newsitem.title: USA: British nanny pleads not guilty to murder charge.
newsitem.headline: British nanny pleads not guilty to murder charge.

text.p: An 18-year-old British nanny plead not guilty on Thursday to a charge of murder in connection with a nine-month-old boy's death from head injuries.

Louise Woodward, who arrived in the United States in June from her home in Chester, England, was ordered held without bail. She is accused of fatally injuring Matthew Eappen in a moment of frustation a week ago.
"She is absolutely no threat to the community or the victim's family," Woodward's defence lawyer Maria Galvagna argued in an unsuccessful effort to get her client's $100,000 bail reduced.
Instead, Judge Conrad Beletzer ordered Woodward held without bail after entering her not guilty plea.
Woodward showed no emotion during the hearing. Her father Gary and British consular officials were in the front row of spectators and immediately left the courtroom without talking to reporters.
Prosecutors said preliminary autopsy results showed the baby's head was struck against a hard, flat object.
